evidence: app/package.json:11 — vite ^8.3.5 devDependency, which is the current latest stable (v8.3.5, 2026-10-21, per npm and vitejs/vite releases)
app/src/main.js:1-32 — ES modules throughout, no legacy module formats or bundler-specific globals
app/server.mjs:1-4 — node: prefixed core imports and ES-module server
app/src/api.js:83-85 — replaceAll/?? / optional chaining: current language level
app/server.mjs:6 — path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) where Node ≥20.11 already offers import.meta.dirname (Node 24 is the runtime per .nvmrc)
latest_apis.rationale: The toolchain is the current stable release and the code is uniformly modern; there is no legacy-era API surface to migrate away from. The only dated idiom is the fileURLToPath dance where import.meta.dirname is now the simpler stable form.

evidence: app/src/api.js:33-47 — fetch with response.ok check and in-memory promise cache; platform-first data loading
app/src/main.js:117-130 — URL + URLSearchParams for all query handling; no hand-rolled query parsing
app/src/main.js:895-913 — history.pushState/popstate SPA navigation instead of a router library
app/src/styles.css:58-61 — :focus-visible; styles.css:344-346 — aspect-ratio; tokens.css custom properties for all theming
app/src/api.js:33-47 — api() accepts no AbortSignal; stale renders are discarded via a renderToken counter (app/src/main.js:44-46) instead of aborting in-flight fetches
app/server.mjs:57-61 — fs.existsSync/fs.statSync (sync) on every request instead of fs/promises
platform.rationale: The app consistently reaches for the platform (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, history API, custom properties, ES modules) and hand-rolls nothing that the platform provides. It stops short of AbortController, which would cancel the bursts of move-detail fetches on game switches rather than just ignoring their results.

evidence: app/package.json:10-13 — zero runtime dependencies; single devDependency is vite
app/src/api.js:56-66 — hand-rolled concurrency limiter instead of pulling a p-limit-style package
app/server.mjs — ~90-line node:http static server instead of express/serve-static
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: nothing ships to the browser but the app's own code, the build tool is the current stable major, and every piece of glue (concurrency limiter, static server, router, escaping) is a small, readable hand-rolled module rather than a dependency.

evidence: app/src/api.js:33-54 — every network call goes through one api() function with a single cache; swapping transport or adding timeouts touches one file
app/src/data.js:5-90 — species/types/generations shape the raw API responses once, behind named loaders with module-level caching
app/src/ui.js:7-41 — card/panel rendering isolated from page logic
app/src/api.js:8-10 — API_BASE_URL resolved in one place from the server-injected global (app/server.mjs:32), so no build-time env coupling
app/src/main.js:840-875 — route table is one function; adding a route is one branch
app/src/main.js:147-347 — ~200 lines of inline HTML template strings in main.js; escaping is opt-in per interpolation (~40 call sites), a standing footgun
app/src/main.js:436-457 — moves panel re-rendered via outerHTML with listeners re-attached on every sort, duplicating the delegation pattern already used at main.js:877
churn_resistance.rationale: Boundaries are genuinely clean: data access, formatting/escaping, UI fragments and routing each live in one module, there is no vite.config and no reliance on Vite internals, so a Vite upgrade (or removal) touches nothing. What it lacks is a safety net: zero type annotations or JSDoc across 130 functions, no app-level tests, and manual escaping discipline at every interpolation.

findings.issue: api() takes no AbortSignal; stale renders are dropped by a renderToken counter (app/src/main.js:44-46) while the underlying requests keep running — a game switch can fire dozens of uncancellable move-detail fetches (loadRowsForGame, app/src/main.js:460-487).
findings.suggestion: Add an optional signal parameter to api() and abort the previous render's requests in renderRoute (AbortController per route render).

findings.issue: Page markup is built from inline template strings where every interpolation must remember escapeHtml/escapeAttr; a new page or a missed escape is a latent XSS bug the team must police by hand.
findings.suggestion: Centralize template building (or add a tiny tagged-template helper that escapes by default), so correctness doesn't depend on discipline at ~40 call sites.

findings.issue: No JSDoc types and no unit tests anywhere in app/ (0 test LOC, 130 functions); refactoring the shared helpers is unverifiable.
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc @typedef for the API response shapes at the data-access boundary (api.js/data.js) and a handful of vitest cases for humanize, latestEnglishFlavor, sortRows and the filters.

findings.issue: path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) where import.meta.dirname has been stable since Node 20.11 (runtime here is Node 24).
Synchronous fs.existsSync/fs.statSync run on every request in the hot path.
findings.suggestion: Use fs.promises.stat and handle the ENOENT rejection; the stream already uses the async API.

findings.issue: Every unknown path is served index.html with HTTP 200; the spec says a 404 status is encouraged where the architecture allows, and it does (the client already renders Not found).
findings.suggestion: For paths that cannot match any client route (e.g. /pokemon/<name>/extra), respond 404; at minimum return 404 for asset-like paths under dist that are missing.

findings.issue: Sorting and game-switching rebuild the whole moves panel via outerHTML and re-attach listeners to every header each time, duplicating work the existing global click delegation (main.js:877) already does for links.
findings.suggestion: Delegate one click handler on the moves panel keyed by data-sort-key, and replace only the affected table's tbody.

findings.issue: sr-only uses the legacy clip: rect(0,0,0,0) technique.
findings.suggestion: clip-path: inset(50%) is the current idiom and behaves better with newer layout.

summary: A lean vanilla JS + Vite 8 app that is squarely current: zero runtime dependencies, the latest stable Vite, and a platform-first data layer (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, history API) with genuinely clean module boundaries that would survive a Vite upgrade untouched. The main aging risks are operational rather than architectural: no AbortController so stale work keeps running, manual escaping at every interpolation, and no types or tests to make future refactors safe.
